brief: A tool caddy with a carry handle and divided bins for screws and bits.

requirements.requirement: A tool caddy: a small carryable cluster of cells holding tools
requirements.evidence: Three cells in a triangle at (0,0), (1,0) and (0,1), with end caps on the open faces and the joints bolted. 16 parts in total, with pliers shown in one bin.

There's a grab handle (accessory:0#1,0#0) on the side of cell (1,0), so you can lift the caddy by its side. A handle across the top, like a classic caddy, couldn't go on: the configurator found nowhere to fit the trinity handle. The configurator only checks fit, so whether the handle holds a loaded caddy isn't checked.
bin:0,0,0 is a full-depth bin with 3 compartments, holding M3 screw and nut piles.
bin:0,1,0 has 3 compartments and bin:1,0,0 has 2, so there's room for bits. They hold nut, standoff and screw piles because the library has no bit item to show.

finish.summary: I built a 3-cell caddy with a side grab handle and three divided full-depth bins: 16 parts, about 1.6 kg of filament. The handle stands off one side wall. A handle that spans the top wasn't possible: the configurator found nowhere to fit one. The last check passed with no rule errors and no parts colliding. It flagged two open faces on cell (1,0) that could still take caps; I didn't check whether those sit beside the handle, and I left them open. One screw pile in the screw bin can't be seen from the angle I viewed it at. The parts library has no screwdriver-bit item to show in the bits bin, so I used nut and standoff piles to stand in for bits.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

parts.name: Grab handle
parts.use: A bar standing off the flat with room for a hand behind it, for a cell or a column that gets moved by its side rather than its top.

parts.name: Trinity handle
parts.use: Reaches across a whole triangle of studs, so a lift is shared between recesses instead of hanging off one, and the cell can be carried loaded.
